title: Companies Act, 2013 — Section 189 (Register of contracts or arrangements in which directors are interested)

content.overview: Section 189 requires every company to keep one or more registers giving separately the particulars of all contracts or arrangements to which section 184 or section 188 applies, in such manner and containing such particulars as may be prescribed. Entries are made within the prescribed time after the Board meeting that approved the contract or arrangement. The register is placed before the next meeting of the Board and signed by all the directors present. The register is kept at the registered office and is open for inspection. Members may take extracts. Failure to maintain the register attracts the penalty provided.
content.glance: Register of contracts/arrangements under ss. 184 and 188; entries after Board approval; placed before next Board meeting and signed by directors present; kept at registered office; open to inspection; extracts allowed.
content.study: Every company shall keep one or more registers giving separately the particulars of all contracts or arrangements to which sub-section (2) of section 184 or section 188 applies, in such manner and containing such particulars as may be prescribed and after entering the particulars, such a register or registers shall be placed before the next meeting of the Board and signed by all the directors present at the meeting. Every director or key managerial personnel shall, within a period of thirty days of his appointment, or relinquishment of his office, as the case may be, disclose to the company the particulars specified in sub-section (1) of section 184 relating to his concern or interest in the other associations which are required to be included in the register. The register shall be kept at the registered office of the company and it shall be open for inspection during business hours. Members may take extracts. The section is a record-keeping duty; the approval of the underlying contract is governed by sections 184 and 188. Current-law framing: confirm the contract is one to which s. 184(2) or s. 188 applies; ensure timely entry and Board presentation; check inspection access.

sections.heading: Scope
sections.body: Register covers contracts or arrangements to which s. 184(2) or s. 188 applies.

sections.heading: Entry and Board Presentation
sections.body: Particulars are entered as prescribed; the register is placed before the next Board meeting and signed by all directors present.

sections.heading: Location and Inspection
sections.body: Kept at the registered office; open for inspection during business hours; members may take extracts.

sections.heading: Relationship to Approval
sections.body: The register records the contract; approval itself is under ss. 184 and 188.

provisions.title: Register of contracts or arrangements in which directors are interested

examples.title: Missing register entry
examples.body: A related-party contract under s. 188 is approved by the Board but never entered in the s. 189 register. The approval route may have been followed, but the record-keeping duty under s. 189 is breached.

examples.title: Inspection
examples.body: A member requests inspection of the register of contracts in which directors are interested during business hours at the registered office. Section 189 requires the company to allow inspection.

hypotheticals.question: Does maintaining the s. 189 register dispense with Board consent under s. 188?
hypotheticals.analysis: No. Section 189 is a register of contracts already governed by ss. 184 and 188. Recording an entry does not replace the need for the substantive approval those sections require.

distinctions.title: Register of interested contracts (s. 189) vs related-party transactions (s. 188)

misconceptions.trap: The register under s. 189 is optional if the contract was approved under s. 188.
misconceptions.correction: Section 189 imposes a separate duty to maintain and present the register for contracts to which s. 184(2) or s. 188 applies.

questionsAndAnswers.question: How should a Section 189 problem be analysed?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: I. Confirm contract falls under s. 184(2) or s. 188. II. Check timely entry and Board presentation. III. Test inspection access. IV. Conclude.

questionsAndAnswers.question: What should submissions contain?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: Contract facts; register status; inspection; precise relief.
